item.title: 1: Daily Halacha: Xmas or Christmas? Yoshke or Jesus?
item.description:
May a Jew say the names Jesus and Christmas, or must one say Xmas and that man? The Rabbi explains the biblical prohibition of mentioning the name of an avodah zarah, why the Vilna Gaon and the Rambam show these names are not included, and which title is forbidden.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada
Part of the Daily Halacha – Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions series.

item.title: 2: Daily Halacha: Wishing a Non-Jew Merry Christmas or Happy New Year
item.description:
Is wishing a non-Jewish colleague a merry Christmas a form of agreeing to the festival? The Rabbi brings the conditions of the Shulhan Arukh for greeting a non-Jew on his festival, why a happy holiday is the easiest way, and why a happy New Year is less of a problem.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada
Clarification from the previous shiur: it is forbidden to say "Christ" when it is used as an adjective of honour. It is permissible to say Christ's College / Trinity Hall / Christchurch, for the same reasons explained that one is allowed to say Christmas.
Part of the Daily Halacha – Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions series.

item.title: 3: Daily Halacha: Presents to Non-Jews and Attending Parties This Season
item.description:
May one give a non-Jewish neighbour or colleague a present for the festival or the New Year, or go to an end-of-December party? The Rabbi brings the Terumat HaDeshen and the Rama on giving a gift before the day, and when staying away from a work party would cause enmity.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 4: Daily Halacha: Entering a Church
item.description:
May a Jew enter a church? The Rabbi explains the prohibition in the Mishnah and its reasons in Rashi and Tosafot, when some poskim allow it to avoid enmity and Hacham Ovadiah did not, and why Rav Moshe Feinstein allowed voting in a church hall.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 5: Daily Halacha: Giving Non-Kosher Wine to a Non-Jew
item.description:
May one buy non-kosher wine as a gift for a non-Jew? The Rabbi explains the Torah prohibition of Yayin Nesekh and the rabbinic Stam Yenam, and why the Rama allows benefit for Ashkenazim while Sepharadim following the Shulhan Arukh are stricter, including a case of great loss.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 6: Daily Halacha: Yayin Mevushal and Drinking Wine with Gentiles
item.description:
Why is cooked wine not affected by the touch of a non-Jew, and does pasteurised wine count? The Rabbi gives the three reasons of the Rishonim, the view of Hacham Ovadiah Yoseph and Rav Moshe Feinstein, and a less known halacha about drinking even kosher wine together at a non-Jewish feast.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada

item.title: 7: Daily Halacha: Wine Touched by Someone Who Does Not Keep Shabbat
item.description:
May one drink kosher wine that was handled by a Jew who publicly desecrates Shabbat? Some argue he counts like a non-Jew for this law. The Rabbi gives three reasons why that view is not followed and leniency is justified, starting with the reasons behind the prohibition on wine touched by non-Jews.
Daily Halacha — Avodah Zarah and December Halachic Common Questions Dayan Daniel Kada
